# Vertebroplasty / Kyphoplasty — Authorization Guide

## CPT Codes — Vertebral Augmentation

| CPT | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 22510 | Percutaneous vertebroplasty (bone biopsy included when performed), 1 vertebral body, unilateral or bilateral injection; cervicothoracic |
| 22511 | Percutaneous vertebroplasty; lumbosacral |
| 22512 | Percutaneous vertebroplasty; each additional cervicothoracic or lumbosacral vertebral body (add-on) |
| 22513 | Percutaneous vertebral augmentation (kyphoplasty), 1 vertebral body, unilateral or bilateral; thoracic |
| 22514 | Percutaneous vertebral augmentation (kyphoplasty); lumbar |
| 22515 | Percutaneous vertebral augmentation; each additional thoracic or lumbar vertebral body (add-on) |
| 72291 | Radiological supervision and interpretation, percutaneous vertebroplasty or vertebral augmentation; under fluoroscopic guidance |
| 72292 | Radiological supervision and interpretation; under CT guidance |

## ICD-10 Diagnosis Codes

| ICD-10 | Description |
| --- | --- |
| M80.08XA | Age-related osteoporosis with current pathological fracture, vertebra(e), initial encounter |
| M80.08XD | Age-related osteoporosis with current pathological fracture, vertebra(e), subsequent encounter |
| M80.88XA | Other osteoporosis with current pathological fracture, vertebra(e), initial encounter |
| M84.58XA | Pathological fracture in neoplastic disease, vertebra(e), initial encounter |
| M48.50XA | Collapsed vertebra, not elsewhere classified, site unspecified, initial encounter |
| M48.52XA | Collapsed vertebra, cervical region, initial encounter |
| M48.54XA | Collapsed vertebra, thoracic region, initial encounter |
| M48.56XA | Collapsed vertebra, lumbar region, initial encounter |

## Standard Payer Requirements

### Medicare (CMS LCD L35050 / A57566)

- Acute or subacute vertebral compression fracture (VCF) — typically within 12 months
- MRI bone marrow edema (STIR or fat-suppressed sequences) confirming acute fracture
- VAS pain score ≥4 or significant functional impairment
- Conservative therapy trial ≥6 weeks (may be waived for severe pain or hospitalized patients)
- Posterior vertebral wall intact (no significant retropulsion)
- Osteoporotic, traumatic, or pathologic (malignant) etiology

### Commercial Payers (Aetna, BCBS, UHC, Cigna)

- Most require MRI confirmation of bone marrow edema
- Conservative therapy trial ≥6 weeks with documented failure
- VAS ≥4 and functional impairment documented
- Some payers limit coverage to fractures within 6 months
- Kyphoplasty: same criteria as vertebroplasty; some require height loss or kyphosis documentation

### Documentation Checklist

- MRI report with STIR/fat-suppressed sequences confirming bone marrow edema
- VAS pain score and Oswestry Disability Index documented
- Conservative therapy documentation (dates, medications, brace use)
- Fracture level(s), height loss percentage, and kyphosis angle
- Bone density (DXA) results if osteoporotic etiology
- Posterior wall integrity confirmed on CT or MRI
